# BOOK 1 of 2: POLLY THE PAGAN: HER LOST LOVE LETTERS (Isabel Anderson, 1922, The Page Company, Boston; foreword by Basil King)

## Frame (editor's note, "The Lost Lady")
- Author Isabel Anderson, a Red Cross nurse, was in Paris on leave, Good Friday night 1918 (spring drive). Ordered to front next morning. Air raid siren; she was in her room on top floor of the Grande Hotel du Nord.
- A small fair-haired American woman, golden hair, big deep blue eyes, arm in sling, in black dress struggling; asked for help. Anderson helped with heavy coat; woman handed her a small morocco bag and ran back for something; said "You go down and I will join you"; never returned. Bomb struck; front door flew open. Anderson went out, then ducked into a "Cave" (wine cellar) till dawn. Hotel top floors ripped open; watchman; several killed. Anderson took the bag (and the woman's bag) to front by Metro.
- Months later in Paris she opened the bag (black morocco) with lock broken. Contents: letters, clipping about mysterious "Russian Prince" under name Kosloff, Red Cross badge, secret service insignia.
- Notices in Paris papers (Le Matin, Paris Herald). Three replies:
  1. Captain T---- F---- (of ---- Regiment): saw woman at Café Russe, Rue des Capuchins, Feb., dining with big blonde foreigner she called Prince; suspicious; followed; Prince put her in taxi to Grande Hotel du Nord; he lost him at a music hall. Suggests she might be American secret service, he German spy.
  2. S---- B---- (American Y.M.C.A. worker): met her on train Amiens-Paris, black morocco bag, dressed as Salvation Army girl; later in Y uniform in Paris, she denied knowing him.
  3. Joseph M----, clerk of Grande Hotel du Nord: she arrived Good Friday evening, arm in sling; papers destroyed in fire.
- Anderson's conclusion: the lady "perhaps was Polly herself."

## PART I: "The Doings and Misdoings of Polly the Pagan"

### Polly's Journal (Steamship Cleopatra, January; Polly is 20)
- Aboard ship returning from Egypt, Mediterranean. Aunt has discovered a Russian Prince aboard; Aunt wants Polly to marry a title. Polly, Checkers (her twin brother; "brothers don't count") and Aunt on the ship. Polly and Prince walked on deck under full moon.
- Polly wore a rainbow negligée with wing sleeves; mistakenly entered wrong stateroom (not No. 26); Prince there, dressed, at porthole. Boat lurched, door swung shut, knob fell off; Prince helped reinstall knob, bowed her out.
- Polly "ashamed," plans to dodge him.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Cleopatra, next morning)
- Calls her "Mademoiselle Hummingbird"; writes broken English with dictionary. Says he did one good action: resisted kissing her. Quotes Wellington at Waterloo. "The vice of the French or the bragging virtue of the English." Says she "make me pairfectly happy." "I like lively American girl, not afraid of anything, not even of wicked man."

### Prince Boris to Polly (following day)
- Calls her "Mademoiselle Avis." She called herself "Polly the Pagan." He mentions "fairy water" and phoenix; "Eve and Adam." Signs "BORIS." "I say you goodbye, naughty girl."

### Polly's Journal (Rome, a week later; Aunt rented upper floor of old palace)
- Roof terrace garden: pansies, violets, huge earthen jars with pink roses, trellis with vines; mockingbird Cæsar in yellow wicker cage. View of St. Peter's dome, Vatican.
- Small room off roof with open fire; tea by candlelight.
- Louisa, pretty Italian maid, brings sealed letter from a "foreign gentleman."

### Prince Boris to Polly ("My leetle Pagan", Rome)
- Asks to come up; sees her worship nature on terrace; compares her to Pan; "I pray civilization may not bring you ruin."

### Journal continued
- Checkers (twin) has little cart and horse; hunts on the Campagna; American slang. Aunt calls them "collusion" twins; Uncle John used to say that. Polly's song "I'm a little prairie flower."
- Polly threw a rose to a man following her (who turned out to be Prince) outside her window. Aunt scandalized; Polly never to go out alone.
- American Secretary (A. D.) brings the Prince, who is introduced. Louisa helps letters.
- Aunt (called "Cart Horse," reddish hair) new artistic clothes; portrait painted by artist Don Peppi (dark, handsome, wild hair).
- Captain Carlo (dashing Italian officer; Roman nose; piercing eyes; some British blood; hunts on Campagna; poor). Gonzaga is rich Spanish diplomat, Marquis; "Pan" = Turkish Ambassador, round-faced, red fez, jewelled rings.
- A. D. (American Diplomat, dark, slender, clean-shaven) gives Polly a ride in his brougham; "love-proof"; they call each other friends.
- Duchess Sermoneta's dance; Prince absent; Aunt says take Louisa hereafter.
- A. D.'s dinner party: Dutch Secretary "Jonkheer Jan" (lanky, tall, blonde); Lord Ronald Charlton, British Secretary, pale and thin; Turkish Ambassador. Polly dislikes Prince; dances with Spanish Marquis (flashing black eyes, curly hair, too fat); spends evening in conservatory.
- A. D. is devoted to a "divorcée" — American woman with Mona Lisa smile, gray cat's eyes, come-hither eye; called "Mona Lisa" / "Madame Mona Lisa" / "Lisa"; "grass widow."
- Dinner at Grand Hotel with big excitable American from Pittsburgh, "Pittsburgo" (Pittsburgo shoots himself later). Gonzaga kissed Polly at table after she pricked him with a pin. Carlo and Gonzaga dispute. Dinner of numberless courses; flowers with electric lights; races, chair-jumping.
- Prince letter: "Mon ange, je t'adore!"; postman's blue letter turned out to be from "gray Miss Mouse."
- Tea; Aunt sleeps; Prince stays for dinner. Charity bazaar at Baronessa Blanc's. Polly calls Prince "tongs" flirt.
- Prince says he is not officially attached to Russian Embassy; best friends are the Turks.
- Louisa (dark-eyed contadina) chatters of royal laundry sent to Milan; calls Aunt "he," Checkers "she," Polly "it."
- **February 14 (St. Valentine's):** flowers from A. D. (via his man "Gilet"). Philopena presents. Carlo with his mother (beautiful). Masked dominoes; Checkers, Peppi, A. D. as Pierrots; Veglione. Polly pushed Pittsburgo into fountain.
- Campagna drives in Checkers' two-wheeled cart with absurd pony; songs ("Pull off your walking coat").
- Checkers: "when I get home I'll show you I'm not afraid of work."
- Prince letter: "Oh, Cleopatra child"; enigma; recalls the steamer.
- Journal: last day of Carnival; Gonzaga sends orchids. Anonymous letter from Italian girl in love with Carlo threatening to kill Polly. Mona Lisa's catty note.
- Confrontation with Mona Lisa: she says "You can let my friend alone"; Polly pretends shy, says she may be congratulated; Mona Lisa tears up/throws A. D.'s photograph into fireplace; "I'll get even with you yet."
- American Ambassador closeted with Aunt about A. D. and Mona.
- Carlo chased Polly's carriage; violets thrown from window.
- Polly with Prince (as "Watson") detect: contadina staring hatred; she is Carlo's gardener's daughter; Carlo in army prison for attending Marquis' dance on sick list; Carlo wants to go to South Africa.
- A. D.'s surprise party for Polly: sign "WELCOME, SURPRISE PARTY," "joyous hand," "joyous eye." Coliseum moonlight with A. D.
- Pittsburgo shot himself in front of portrait of Italian singer. Polly had worn his ring for a time.
- American Embassy dinner (gold plates). Ambassador; Polly pumps for Mona info. Princess Pallavicini's reception. Aunt prefers titled foreigner.
- Gonzaga; Boris declares he'll follow her around Europe; Polly bets Checkers a hat she'd make Boris propose.

### Prince Boris to Polly ("Darling Miss")
- Threatens bears; "furia francesa"; D'Artagnan; handkerchief of Polly's lost.

### Journal (Rome, March)
- Polly won the hat from Checkers: Prince proposed; she refused. He: "I love Pagans. I meet you in Paris."
- Leaving Rome for Sorrento. A. D. wants to spend Sunday at Sorrento. Carlo wants to come; she refuses.
- Gonzaga: "my mother says me marry my cousin, a Spanish countess."
- Roman season over.

## PART II: "Court and Courting"

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, March)
- Easter greetings; Prince seen outside her palazzo; Alban mountains picnic: Frascati, Tusculum.

### Polly to A. D. (Sorrento, March)
- Olives: "Ship olives to Park and Tilford, New York." Octopus at Naples (siren's wrath). Neapolitan singer; castanets. Picnic at Frascati with Pan, Prince, Jan, Sybil (Polly's friend, straight black hair, dark blue flirtatious eyes).
- Checkers would give old boots to see A. D.

### A. D. Telegram (April): "I am coming to brave the wrath of one little siren tomorrow." (Footnote: telephone-transmitted.)

### Polly to A. D. (Sorrento, April)
- Gold pen gift; Aunt calls her "Pliny." Studying Roman history (Etruscans, Sabines, Gauls, Hannibal, Goths, Charlemagne, Countess Mathilde).
- Checkers got anonymous letter from "Brown Eyes" (Polly's fake).

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, May)
- Florence memories: Fiesole, church above valley, cypress photograph, pastry cook. Gift: baby Leo pin (lion of St. Mark's).
- Garden party at Spanish Embassy, Palazzo Barberini. Lost the "little ghost" among flowers. Prince, Gonzaga, A. D. champagne.
- Requests photograph of drawing of Polly by Signor Rossi.

### Polly to A. D. (Florence, June)
- Memories: Cascine, Boboli, Fiesole, monks hiding faces. "L'amour fait passer le temps; le temps fait passer l'amour!" Wears lion on chain. Next Sunday in Venice.

### A. D. to Polly (Venice, June)
- St. Mark's; Grand Canal; Charlton dined; fête; "Stephanie" steamer; gondoliers.

### Polly to A. D. (Bayreuth, July)
- Gondola sand-bar night; Aunt angry; sudden Wagner tickets. Aunt wants her to marry Prince.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, July)
- Station; Gilet laughing at urchins.

### Polly to A. D. (Bayreuth, July)
- Fair in small town; bronze horses of St. Mark's (history); Tintoretto; Aunt has auburn hair.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, July)
- Jonkheer Jan's house warming; Falconieri Palace; royal procession; American Admiral; Count L.'s reception; birreria; Prince and German Counsellor.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, July)
- Prince dropped in with Polly's letter; A. D. jealous. Asturia expedition: carriage stuck in bog; Prince deserted, leaving Charlton and A. D.; A. D. wrapped in newspaper (Daily Chronicle). "I have begun to dislike him."

### Polly to A. D. (Bayreuth, July)
- Siegfried, Valkyrie, Rhinegold. Next: Baden Baden, Hague, England, Paris.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, July)
- Grand review; King; Queen; bersaglieri; Bracciano castle (Odescalchi).
- **Opera house Costanzi fire** (gala night, masked ball, blue flame along wire; orchestra played Royal March; firemen; fire broke out again; scorched coats).
- Dining with Prince; "we do not speak of you."

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, July)
- Girandola fireworks at Piazza del Popolo; royal party; Mr. Dooley quote.

### Polly to A. D. (Baden Baden, July)
- Checkers dictating: "I love you just as much as ever, dearest A. D.--Do you love me? Will you be mine?" Beer garden bicycle performer. Silver gondola gift.

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, July)
- Cure; silver gondola; Orvieto cathedral; Minister of Foreign Affairs receptions; Turkish Ambassador and Greek Chargé.
- Prince attacked French secretary at dinner.
- Festival of Assumption; contadini.

### Polly to A. D. (Baden-Baden, August)
- Second proposal (Gonzaga, by letter); she refused; Countess cousin. Captain Carlo in South Africa. Prince writes Aunt. Polly considers Prince.
- Peppi leaves for Rome; lost boots, cane, overcoat.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome): "THE DIARY OF A DAY'S DOINGS" (leaflet "An August Daily"; "Dedicated ... to Miss Pollykins"). Egg-opener; proposals of marriage answered by printed forms. "Will you subscribe?"

### Polly to A. D. (The Hague, August)
- Trip mishaps: caboose broke on bridge; Orient Express; Louisa lost ticket; Strasbourg; Brussels Gallery Wiertz; **stranger kissed Polly at Brussels station**; Checkers stranded for 3 francs, cabby, banker; "Sensation Captain."
- Aunt drinks to Peppi.

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, August)
- Your gondola in my pocket. Dinner at American Embassy memories. Spanish Marquis looked suspicious; Don Carlo; gardener's daughter followed to South Africa.

### Polly to A. D. (The Hague, August)
- Hotels: no rooms; "Why, it is a big one!" House in the Woods; Delft ware; Jonkheer Jan's parents. Homesick (nearly a year away). "There's a kiss for you here somewhere."

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, August)
- Charlton ill, joined cure; Charlton hoped they'd like each other. Blotter token. Mr. Dooley quote.

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, August)
- Prince of Naples engaged. Boris departing for Paris; Boris fought duel with Gonzaga (scratched); woman's name rumored.

### Polly to A. D. (London, September)
- Half Moon Street, Easthope's lodgings; white pinks; "Prince writes Aunt he will join us in Paris." Duel question.

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, September)
- Lodgings described; postman's rap; cab whistles; Lansdowne Passage; one-eyed sweeper; **silver broom** gift.

### Polly to A. D. (London, September)
- Checkers' "Great Mash Act"; red roses; broom; picture in frame; "gorgeous" misspelt.

### A. D. to Polly (Monte Catini, September)
- Lucca excursion; Holy Image of Lucca ship story; P.S. Ambassador refused leave to Paris.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, September)
- Rome preparing for tourists; walk from Quattro Fontane; Jan visit; Frascati; Leicestershire; Checkers' letter urging business.

### Polly to A. D. (Leicestershire, October)
- Carlton Curlieu Hall, Kibworth; Oliver Cromwell's room; Honorable Violet; hunt; fox found in hay mow; brush given to her.

### Polly to A. D. (Leicestershire, October)
- Confession: dark handsome Oxford man saw A. D.'s photo in watch; she said A. D. was her older brother. "Men are April when they woo..." (Aunt).

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, October)
- "Spice" forbidden in diet; Peppi with goose; trapeze girl looks like Mona Lisa; asks her to sail home via Naples.

### Polly to A. D. (Leicestershire, October)
- Gypsy fortune: gray-eyed woman may give trouble; handsome man in south will disappoint. Prince joining in Paris.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, October)
- Asks if gypsy mentioned blond Russian Prince. "Why do you let the Prince join you in Paris?"

### Telegrams (Oct.): Polly "Can't you stand a little teasing?"; A.D. "Not from you... you are meeting the Prince in Paris"; Polly "What can you expect when I haven't seen you"; A.D. "More than I am getting"; Polly "Aren't you unreasonable?"; A.D. "I think not"; Polly "?"; A.D. "!"; Polly "."

## PART III: "Uncertainty"

### Cable A. D. (Rome, November): "Will you marry me? ... Heaven or Hell?" Cable Polly (New York): "Call it Heaven."

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, November)
- Quarrel; "Mona Lisa has disappeared from my life"; recounts their history since Rome (Coliseum, Carnival Veglione, Sorrento, Venice gondola); Tennyson quote.

### Polly to A. D. (New York, November)
- Aunt won't openly oppose; pretends not engaged; remarks about Boris. Paris: Boris's Russian wolf hound; Boris locked lift door: "Once before you were in my power, in the stateroom on the Cleopatra... Now I got dog, no fool any more." Polly: "I came here to eat and not to make love." Escaped; Aunt insisted all go to circus with him. Bois jumping horses. Luxembourg sphinx sculpture; Polly quoted poem. Boris says Polly was cause of duel.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, November)
- Proposes announcing engagement; can't come home yet (Charlton seriously ill). Describes St. Peter's visit with Charlton; Peppi's old apartment.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Paris, December): followed her to Paris; offers sables, Urals jewels, Moscow; "Be my Princess."

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, December): Cable re announcing; Checkers sent engagement book; Pan's toast; Charlton's warm congratulations; will hurry home.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Moscow, December): Russian culture; Ivan the Terrible; Aunt wrote him to come to New York; "American Diplomat... went often to the circus, to see pretty girl... like your enemy, the lady of the gray eyes."

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, December): desk memories; ruins of Campagna.

### Polly to A. D. (Black Horse Farm on the Hudson, December): Colonial house; Chippendale; John Sullivan, bull pup. Honeymoon idea. P.S. asks about Mona successor.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, December): Court reception at Quirinal described; Highland fling with umbrellas; asks her not to delay announcing.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Moscow, December): silver plate; Peppi's "title" comment; "Hummingbird welcome me."

### Polly to A. D. (Christmas Morning, Black Horse Farm): diamond engagement ring in stocking; cuff links sent; Aunt wants Peppi news; father sent letter from California.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, Christmas Day): cuff-links on breakfast tray; church decorations; silk hat knocked by worshipper (Gilet's pride).

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, Dec. 31): Peppi painting behind locked doors; calls A. D. "birdcage." 

### Polly to A. D. (New York, Dec. 31): Sybil visiting; hummingbird-colored frock; Sybil wants them to have a thousand children; Polly asked Aunt to announce.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, New Year's Day): Peppi's supper; Charlton's death on New Year's Day; A. D. sends resignation; "Hip-hip-hurrah."

### Polly to A. D. (New York, January): photo kissed; Lord Ronald Charlton's death; "Cable me when you leave."

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, January): plan: May wedding, Black Horse Farm, then cruise South (Spanish Main, Horn). Sketch of his room with altar; "Mecca." Court Ball opened by him with Grand Master's daughter; Queen; Mona Lisa back in Rome.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Moscow, February): "My little blond rose"; hints Mona Lisa.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, February): Embassy Ball with King and Queen; Quadrille d'honneur; Gilet signals band; Royal March; Star Spangled Banner; chestnut horse named "Mona Lisa" by Peppi (at Ferini's near Borghese villa).

### Polly to A. D. (New York, February): Aunt busy with charities; Boris coming; Polly announced engagement in papers herself.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, February): Jan plays piano at Peppi's; carries last letter in pocket.

### Polly to A. D. (Black Horse Farm, March): snow; dressed in rubber boots driving four horses.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Rome, March): "American Secretary... goes the other way"; "Carthorse".

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, March): Austrian Embassy Ball; rainbow ride; "I follow your pesky Prince!"

### Polly to A. D. (New York, March): 21 years old; denounces Mona Lisa "gray cat's eyes"; Aunt inserted denial of engagement; birthday gifts: bedroom slippers, work-bag, silver coffee pot (from Checkers); Mr. French (business man), safe deposit tin box; bought ring for Sybil; A.D. sent great pearl on a chain.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, March): photos of Campagna meets; Carnival; King's birthday (Persian Ambassador); Foreign Office dinner; "Mona Lisa" toast dispute: Peppi toasted "To Mona Lisa!"; Pan toasted "Miss Polly"; Mona gave imitation pansy; St. Mark lion on Boris's chain (ruby eyes) — A. D. questioned Boris; Boris said "Maybe, who knows?"; Boris sailed for New York. A. D. plans to flirt with Mona.

### Prince Boris to Polly (New York, March telegram): "Shall be with you tomorrow."

### Polly to A. D. (New York, March): "I'm getting desperate." Prince arrives tomorrow.

### Polly cable (April 1): "Breaking my engagement for reasons you can no doubt surmise."

## PART IV: "The Prince in Pursuit"

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, April 1): found cable; telephoned Lisa (Mona), she said come over; Lisa knows no reason.

### A. D. cable (April 1 evening): "April Fool!"

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, April 2): Polly's apology cable; new Ambassador confirmed; Peppi's old masters; copies boxed for Boris, address on New York's east side.

### Polly to A. D. (New York, April): Aunt takes them to Louisville races, then Canada. Lost lion in Paris; didn't know Boris had it. Wedding preparations; presents; invitations.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, April): new Secretary coming; wedding end of May. Peppi's party at Villa Olivia; danced with Mona Virginia reel.

### Prince Boris to Polly (Washington, April): Americans described; "Excuse my funs."

### Polly to A. D. (Louisville, Ky., April): Derby: Speed Limit won; Sybil and Checkers mock engagement ("trial hitch"), now real. Mrs. Courtney's house; Boris's fall from horse; scar; secret stairway. Aunt adamant. Cablegram suggesting May 31.

### A. D. to Polly (Rome, April): two telegrams; "How about May 31?"; Checkers and Sybil congratulations.

### Polly to A. D. (New York, May): invitations mailed; Rector (father's old friend) will perform ceremony; church, azaleas; going to Canada.

### Polly's journal "Island Lake, Algonquin Park, Canada": guides; canoe capsized; Boris rescued her; kissed hand; Checkers "Bully!"; Prince "Bozhe moi!"; Aunt "This box has got soap! Not eggs!"; Boris's guide hired to tip canoe for "heroic rescue"; Boris tried kissing her in tent; guide intervened; Boris's secret letters under other name; Polly suspects antique-dealer. Fourth day: Rock Lake, bonfire.

### A. D. to Polly (En route, May): Rome farewell; King's audience (21:30); Mt. Cenis; Peppi and Mona married in Rome (with Gonzaga, Pan, Jan as witnesses); Mona's visit: "Your little Polly is very sweet... I've made up my mind to something."

### A. D. to Polly (London, May): crossing; Folkestone; Charing Cross; Curzon Street sweeper; broom returned.

### Polly to A. D. (En route, May): Aunt's refusal; Polly told Aunt about rector; "Are you crazy?"

### A. D. to Polly (Washington, May): arrived; Father greeted him.

### Polly to A. D. (En route, May): Montreal; acceptances in Aunt's lap; **US border search: officials sought a foreigner stealing Old Masters; "Kosloff"** — Boris's name on his letters.

### Telegram Polly (Washington): "We reach New York the 28th... Much love. POLLY."

### Prince Boris to Polly (New York, May): asks to explain pictures and Kosloff.

### A. D. to Polly (Washington, May): called Russian Embassy; Ambassador guarded; Boris dined at German Embassy; Boris sold Peppi's copies on commission; Peppi warned to cease dealings with Boris. Postscript: arriving New York May 30.

### Polly's Last Entry (May 31, early morning): Boris disguised as nun ("Sister Beatrice") visited on May 30; wanted her to elope on Carpathia; threatened; left with Aunt; Aunt elopes with Boris; **package bomb** left on vestibule; A. D. dropped it in pantry pail of water ("set for one o'clock"); Checkers chased to dock; Carpathia sailed 1:30; Aunt returned on pilot boat; Boris slunk off.

### A. D. to Polly (An hour before the wedding, May 31): "Until noon and then...."

## CONCLUSION (Anderson)
- Letters end; she surmises the wedding happened. Clipping (from American paper) about a Russian Prince, forger/spy in Paris, arrested while lunching with an American lady who had earlier distrust; dictagraph; food packages to Russian prisoners.
- Anderson recalls: arrested Prince at restaurant; blonde woman with right arm injured; Head waiter said Prince frequented; "Who is the lady?" "American." Anderson couldn't trace Boris.

# "THE LADY FOUND" (Polly's letter to Anderson)
- Polly: "Dear Friend of Good Friday Night." She got out on Bordeaux train to America.
- A. D. went to Russia with American Red Cross; imprisoned; Boris released in Paris, now in high standing with Soviets in Moscow.
- Polly starting for Europe to meet A. D. at frontier.
- Gives permission to publish; wants Americans warned about citizens imprisoned abroad.
- Signed: POLLY THE PAGAN. END.

# BOOK 2 of 2: "US, AND OUR CHARGE" (Amy Le Feuvre; Religious Tract Society, London; frontispiece "ARE YOU ALL SAFE?")

## Characters
- Narrator: **Grisel** (Grizzy, "Gristle"; eldest daughter; keeps the diary; mother Grace Noble; "Hold fast" charge).
- **Denys Marjoribanks** (eldest boy, Head of Family; "Grand-duke's face"; wants to be soldier/artillery; H.F. tattoo; Woolwich).
- **Aylwin** (second boy; wiseacre; wants Flying Corps; H.F. tattoo).
- **Lynette** (sister, harum-scarum, wild; "Scaramouche"; H.F. tattooed on her foot; hits when woken).
- **Puff** (youngest, ~stammering "fwogs"; calls grandfather "Gruffy"; "gempleum" = gentleman).
- **Father**: Rector, died of double pneumonia (funeral in blizzard). Last words: "Grisel—remember—tell the boys—I charge you—Hold fast! Hold fast!—" Father's mother-in-law Lady Louisa Noble (pedigree claim).
- **Mother**: Grace Noble; "Rosebud" doll grave ("destroyed by Fluffie's puppies"); miniature pendant from Aunt Grisel.
- **Mr. Adamson**: father's lawyer (school friend of father).
- **Aunt Caroline** (died March); **Aunt Mildred** (married doctor, India).
- **Grandfather**: Colonel Noble, of Bantock Hall near Killochan (Scotland), gout, fierce eyebrows, red face, white moustache, twinkly eyes; calls them "Bantam" (Puff) "young Jackanapes."
- **Aunt Isobel** (Mrs. Crichton, widow; tall, grey satin, diamonds; cold but moving; "Good little Grisel").
- **Peggy**: old nurse of mother; Scots dialect; "Miss Grace's bairns."
- **Jenkins**: butler (falls on stairs with tray).
- **Ambrose**: old coachman; **Slapper**: old sheep (cob); **Andy**: donkey at Rectory.
- **Davey**: under-gardener, ex-Navy; **Keith**: gardener.
- **Pat Douglas**: Irish boy, Miss Douglas's nephew, merry, "Oirish," sailing boat; saved from cliff; cave on island; Testament; killed in France.
- **Miss Douglas**: Pat's aunt (grey-haired, rides).
- **Miss Garton**: governess, tall, beautiful, dark eyes, fair hair; six brothers; "Hold fast to a strong and loving Hand"; her brother going to front.
- **Aunt Grisel** (Lady Grisel, mother's aunt, godmother; widow; Mr. Dick (husband) died in India; silver grey hair; aviary; "Hoots!"; miniature).
- **Miss Fawcett** (Lydia Fawcett): ex-London hospital matron, runs hospital at Aunt Grisel's.
- **Gervas Carrington**: Lincolnshire friend, lungs/gas poisoned, Sandhurst.
- **Captain Rogers**: Lincolnshire tutor/friend.
- **Major Streatfield**: Chief Constable.
- **David Grier**: coastguardsman, whisky smell, pipe scratched.
- **Captain Hugh Gordon**: aeroplane pilot.
- **Tom Bradley**: Lincolnshire League member.
- Gaps: Puff's pony promised by grandfather.
- Other: Dr. Lane (doctor), Mr. Scammell (vicar), Andy, Fluffie, Gruffy.

## Chapter I: A Bomb-Shell
- Father dead (Aunt Caroline died March; Aunt Mildred India). Father: "Grisel—remember—tell the boys." Mr. Adamson; insurance £2,000 (~£80-90 income). Five children: Grisel, Denys, Aylwin, Lynette, Puff.
- Council in schoolroom; "minors." Letter from grandfather Colonel Noble invites them Monday to Bantock Hall.
- Denys's letter: "D. MARJORIBANKS, THE HEAD OF THE FAMILY." Postscripts from each: Grisel ("darling mother was your daughter"), Aylwin ("rough lines on fellows of the Fifth Form"), Lynette ("General Walton... high-jinks"), Puff ("fwogs").
- Imagined houses (Denys: rugged tower; Aylwin: dungeon; Lynette: garden; Grisel: cold town house; Puff: big hall).
- Puff: "God will live in his house... Not in wicked people's houses."

## Chapter II: Our New Home
- Last Sunday; goodbyes; "Hold fast" discussion with concordance & Bible verses: "Hold fast that which is good"; "Hold fast the form of sound words"; "That which ye have already hold fast till I come"; "Hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown." Chosen charge: "Hold fast that which is good."
- Journey: Glasgow; Killochan station (stationmaster); brougham; Aunt Isobel; Peggy; nursery wing with green baize door.
- Lovely sea view next morning; beach; Lynette reads Daily Light.
- Denys: "I'll speak to my grandfather"; library waiting.

## Chapter III: We Explore
